sentences.text: 1  2  2025:KER:32671  JUDGMENT Dated this the 8th day of April, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.360/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.9.2011.

According to the petitioner, on 25.9.2011, at about 8 p.m., while he was travelling in a motor cycle, a tourist bus driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10, B1, and C1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs..4,38,550/- rounded to Rs.4,39,000/-
and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9.

Heard Sri. Mohammed Salahudhin, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant,
and Sri.P.M.M. Najeeb Khan, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

sentences.text: 10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as an autorickshaw driver earning Rs.12,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the 2011 will come to Rs.8000/-.

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the accident being in the year 2011 his notional income is fixed at Rs.11,000/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Type III open fracture both bones of right leg, lacerated wound 15x7x5 cms on right knee."
He was treated as inpatient for 83 days 13.

As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the petitioner suffered 36%
permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 36%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 23 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 2025:KER:32671 SCC 121].

In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.11,97,504/-.
15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.24,000/- being the income for 6 months @ Rs.4,000/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 9 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.99,000/-
(11,000x 9 months).
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.35,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.15,000/- was awarded, towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2,500/- and towards 'transport to hospital', Rs.1,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner,

sentences.text: 17. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 83 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment 2025:KER:32671 undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life', 'extra nourishment' and 'transportation expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.60,000/-,
Rs.40,000/-, Rs.10000/- and Rs.3000/- respectively.
18.

Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.14,59,514/-
rounded to Rs.14,59,550/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
